races.name: Zyn Pole Position EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Ancestor
runners_data.note: William Haggas sends this 3yo back to Haydock where he won over 10f on Good going last time; natural front-runner with a clean lead guaranteed here, his 137lb weight is notable but T14 form of 10/50 is solid and Tom Marquand rides with confidence from the front — the uncontested lead is his biggest asset.

runners_data.name: Golden Caviar
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's hold-up performer returns quickly on just 8 days rest after two consecutive fifth-place finishes — 0W0P in recent form and limited impact from the back in a slow-run three-horse race where he will need a true gallop to make his late effort count; T14 at 1/18 is modest.

runners_data.name: Tropical Sands
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's lightly-raced 3yo steps up markedly in trip to 1m2f having only run twice, most recently 57 days ago on Soft ground — the step to Good turf and extra furlong is unexplored territory, but the freshener and lightly-raced profile mean this horse carries the most upside unknown, with Clifford Lee looking to exploit any pace collapse in the straight.

races.paceDynamic: Ancestor is the sole confirmed front-runner in a three-horse field and will lead from the outset without any meaningful challenge for the lead, setting whatever tempo William Haggas and Tom Marquand choose over this 1m2f trip on Good ground. Golden Caviar and Tropical Sands are both held-up or unknown-style horses with no natural pace to contest early position, meaning Ancestor can dictate a controlled, measured gallop from flag to finish. At Good going on a flat Haydock track, an uncontested leader who can control fractions and quicken from the front is in an enviable tactical position, particularly with a 30-day freshener behind him and a solid form line of 1-4 over 10 furlongs. This race shape overwhelmingly favours the front-running profile — a horse leading at its own pace, conserving energy, and forcing the closers to come from off a slow or steady pace rather than being delivered into a truly run race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ancestor Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Ancestor dictates a controlled tempo throughout and kicks clear in the straight, denying the hold-up horses a true gallop to close into.
scenarios.body: Ancestor leads every yard at a pace of Marquand's choosing, and with only two rivals who both lack early speed, the closers face the worst possible scenario — chasing a fresh, well-rated leader who has never been asked a question. Ancestor's 2/2 record at similar going and winning form over this course distance make him the primary beneficiary of his own pace control.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Late
scenarios.trigger: If Ancestor sets a genuinely strong gallop and ties himself up in the final furlong, allowing one of the hold-up runners to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: A testing pace from the front would see Ancestor's stamina reserves tested over 1m2f, and either Golden Caviar or Tropical Sands could close off a fast pace on Good ground if the fractions have been honest throughout. Tropical Sands, with his softer-ground form and lightly-raced profile, may be the unexposed one capable of a late lunge if conditions encourage a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tropical Sands Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If Tropical Sands proves significantly better than his bare form suggests and has improved markedly during a 57-day absence with stamina found at this longer trip.
scenarios.body: Lightly raced at just two starts, Tropical Sands is an unknown quantity stepping up to 1m2f for Ed Walker, a trainer in solid 10/38 form, and a first run on Good turf could unlock improvement. If the class ceiling is higher than his current OR of 120 implies, he can close into a slow-run race and surprise, though he must overcome a completely open form profile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Into Tactical
scenarios.trigger: If Marquand elects not to bowl along and the race crawls, producing a sprint finish that levels the playing field for all three.
scenarios.body: A very slow pace would theoretically remove Ancestor's advantage and turn this into a sprint at the death, but with Ancestor's natural lead style and Haggas unlikely to invite pressure by dawdling, this shape is the least probable outcome in the field.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Ancestor bowls along freely or gets restrained by Marquand — any significant slowdown in the opening half-mile fundamentally changes the chance of Golden Caviar and Tropical Sands closing late.
Tropical Sands is 57 days between runs and steps up notably in trip; watch the paddock closely for any signs of tension or condition concerns that could blunt his performance on this Good surface.

Golden Caviar's T14 figure of 1/18 for Ed Dunlop is a concern — horses from this stable in current form have underperformed, and a hold-up horse in a three-runner race where the pace may be controlled is tactically compromised.

With only three runners, any incident or stumble early is magnified — watch the initial stalls break, particularly Tropical Sands (stall draw impact in small fields can be decisive on a flat, turning track like Haydock).

Monitor the going reports through the afternoon card — multiple races confirm Good across all distances at Haydock today, which consistently favours Ancestor's profile based on his sim-going record of 2/2.

races.name: Zyn In The Moment Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dream Harder
runners_data.note: Won last time out 8 days ago over 1m2f on good going for yard in decent form (T14: 2/17); genuine hold-up horse who will need to be produced late, and at 1m6f the extra stamina test may suit — sim-going figures show 2 wins from 11 on similar ground.|
runners_data.comment: Dream Harder won last time out and returns fit on just eight days' rest, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour. He carries 157 lb on a mark of 72, but his profile makes him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Fast Fred
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with good-ground form who placed over 1m2f last time; the step to 1m6f is a query given all five history runs are at shorter, but he tracks pace well and Miss Pippa Brown claims 3lbs helping the handicap equation.|
runners_data.comment: Fast Fred ran a fine second last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, making him a genuine danger; the concern is that he has found only one winner in his last six starts, suggesting consistency could let him down.

runners_data.name: Caph Star
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type that has placed in five of last six; all recent runs at 10-11f suggest this 1m6f trip is a genuine distance question, though good-going handler and in-form stable (T14: 1/5) give confidence in the stable's targeting.|
runners_data.comment: Caph Star arrives in fine fettle on 15 days' rest, and his recent string of placed efforts — third two starts back and runner-up last time out — marks him as a consistent threat; the chief concern is whether he can convert that place form into a win carrying 155 lb.

runners_data.name: Clansman
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the race, last won over 1m6f on the all-weather and has won over 1m2f on the same surface; trainer has had no winners in the last 14 days (0/10) and 41 days off track is a mild flag, but uncontested lead is a significant tactical asset.|
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner two starts back but unplaced last time out, and 41 days on the sidelines adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and his speed rating offers mild encouragement, though 152 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Made All
runners_data.note: Horse with a name suggesting front-running but actually a hold-up type; five of five recent runs are placed/third, showing consistency without winning — good-going trips of 1m4f-1m6f suit, and amateur jockey Rebecca Hitchen claims 5lbs.|
runners_data.comment: Made All has shown consistency with back-to-back thirds in his most recent starts, but a winner five starts back and unplaced efforts in between suggest he's a tricky conveyance; going experience helps, though his 151 lb burden is a significant ask at a rating of 70.

runners_data.name: Arrange
runners_data.note: Solid recent form with two seconds at 1m6f on good ground, so the trip and going are right; however this is a natural closer who — with more hold-up horses than the map can seat at the rear — is unlikely to get a fully detached berth, tempering confidence in its chance despite the appealing form line.|
runners_data.comment: Arrange has been knocking persistently on the door, finishing second in each of her last two starts, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — the main concern is whether she can finally convert, having been winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Edward Sexton
runners_data.note: 109 days off the track is a significant freshness concern, and all recent runs on the all-weather (Stanmore) with little evidence of good-ground turf form (sim-going: 2/9, 1W1P); like Arrange it is a hold-up type that cannot count on its favoured position in this race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, all finishing sixth or seventh, Edward Sexton has been consistently below par and returns after a 109-day break carrying 146 lb — with our figures ranking him seventh of eight, it is hard to make a case for him here.

runners_data.name: Havachoc
runners_data.note: Consistent frame-hunter with four placings in last five starts, mainly on the all-weather; the one good-ground run produced a placing at 1m2f so going is fine, but this is the lowest-rated runner (OR 58) and will need everything to go right from a prominent pitch.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a fourth last time out following a string of minor positions, Havachoc is hard to fancy ranked bottom of the field on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, but offers little encouragement at the weights.

races.paceDynamic: Clansman is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead in an 8-runner field, will dictate from the front at a pace entirely of his own choosing over 1m6f on good ground. Fast Fred, Caph Star, and Havachoc are all prominent types who will compete for early position behind him, creating a natural bunching effect in the first three or four lengths. The field holds more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Arrange and Edward Sexton are genuine closers by inclination but have been mapped to midfield because Dream Harder and Made All already occupy the natural back positions, meaning Arrange and Edward Sexton are unlikely to get the true last-off-the-bridle berth they prefer. With Clansman able to control tempo unchallenged and the good ground unlikely to produce extremes of pace, this shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently, conserve energy through the middle stages, and produce a sustained late effort — making prominent racers with proven good-ground form the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clansman Controls, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Clansman leads at a measured, uncontested gallop and prominent pursuers Fast Fred, Caph Star, or Havachoc track him closely throughout.
scenarios.body: Clansman sets a sustainable tempo that allows prominent horses to travel on his heels without over-exerting, and when the pace lifts turning for home those with the best cruising positions have first run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In Late
scenarios.trigger: If Clansman's pace is genuinely slow early and the field compresses, gifting Dream Harder or Made All a free passage from behind.
scenarios.body: A sluggish gallop can compress the race into the final three furlongs, and horses who had ridden quietly off the pace — particularly Dream Harder who has form in this grade — can produce a powerful sustained finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Clansman Front-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Clansman dictates a moderate, relaxed pace and simply never relinquishes the lead as stamina becomes the primary test.
scenarios.body: On good ground over 1m6f, an uncontested front-runner who has already won over course-and-distance equivalent trips on the all-weather can be very difficult to reel in when he controls every yard; his rivals are all amateur-ridden, adding a tactical uncertainty.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Land Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Arrange or Edward Sexton manage to secure a wider but genuinely detached position and the pace surprisingly quickens sharply in the straight.
scenarios.body: This shape requires both horses to race against their mapped position and for the race to develop in an unusual way; Arrange has decent recent form at 1m6f on good ground including two placed efforts, but the style-fit discount and redistribution tag make this a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Clansman's uncontested lead is the race's defining tactical factor — watch whether he bowls along at a genuine gallop or idles in front, as the entire field's finishing positions depend on the tempo he sets.|

Fast Fred and Caph Star will both want to sit second or third early; if they crowd each other or are pushed wider than ideal in the opening furlongs, their energy expenditure could blunt their finish.|

Arrange has the best course form in the field (two seconds at 1m6f good ground) but cannot guarantee its natural hold-up berth — watch where Eireann Cagney actually settles, as a forced prominent position would undermine its chance significantly.|
Edward Sexton returns after 109 days off the track for Gary & Josh Moore, who show a modest 1/19 in the last 14 days; monitor in-running to see whether the layoff has left it short of peak fitness.|

Dream Harder arrives just 8 days after a win, which is a quick turnaround — watch whether it travels with the same fluency as last time or shows signs of tiredness in the final two furlongs after a busy schedule.|

races.name: Zyn Pacesetter Cup Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: God Given Talent
runners_data.note: William Haggas's 2yo is in excellent form — a recent win at 6f on Good going gives strong course-and-conditions confidence, and stepping back to 5f for a prominent racer with Tom Marquand aboard should suit; three-from-three on similar ground is a key credential here.
runners_data.comment: God Given Talent won three starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with 21 days between runs leaving him fresh enough to deliver; the concern is that his last two outings have both disappointed.

runners_data.name: Dance A Jig
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly has twice placed at this trip on Good going and brings solid prominent-racer credentials, though 51 days off the track is worth monitoring; Hector Crouch takes over in the saddle and the step back to 5f aligns with her best form.
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in recent starts, Dance A Jig lines up as the top-rated runner here and brings solid placed form to today's trip; yet to land a win from his last three, the 51-day absence is the one query, though connections saddle him with 135 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Jaijai
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner with five runs on Good ground and a record of 1 win and 3 places from those, Jaijai is ideally drawn to dictate a controlled pace; Sean Levey should enjoy an uncontested lead from the off, making her the pivotal horse around which this entire race shape is built.
runners_data.comment: Jaijai brings solid recent form — a winner three starts back and second two starts back — and has experience of today's trip and conditions, carrying 131 lb from stall 3; the unplaced effort last time out is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Undercover Affair
runners_data.note: David Evans's juvenile has a lively profile — a 5f winner on Good going — but as a natural front-runner who cannot get to the lead against Jaijai, she is likely to race in a position behind her preferred slot; the 3lb claimer Ryan Kavanagh adds further uncertainty, and the style mismatch tempers confidence in her finding her best form here.
runners_data.comment: Undercover Affair won two starts back and was third three starts back, with two wins in his last six starts, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions carrying 129 lb; the main risk is an eighth last time out suggesting he needs to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Rotelle
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes won with this filly on her last start over 5f on Good going and she is another who naturally wants to race prominently, yet with Jaijai ahead of her she faces a similar squeeze to Undercover Affair; a positive trainer stat of 0/12 over the past 14 days is a mild flag, though the form profile on this surface is encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Rotelle won two starts back but was beaten well last time out, and he ranks last on our figures here; he has run over today's trip and going, and draw one is noted, but it's hard to fancy at these weights against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Casino Star
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's 2yo has placed twice at this trip and is competent on Good ground, but as a prominent type redistributed to a hold-up position she is the least likely to get a race shape that suits; Clifford Lee rides and the horse simply may not get the ground she needs from the rear in what should be a steady-tempo affair.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts despite a couple of placed efforts, Casino Star has run over today's trip and going before and steps in from stall two carrying 124 lb — modest profile on our figures, though those seconds suggest he's rarely far away.

races.paceDynamic: Jaijai is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no natural pace rival to challenge her, Sean Levey should be able to dictate a controlled, even gallop from the five-furlong start on Good turf at Haydock. God Given Talent and Dance A Jig are the genuine prominent horses best placed to track her through the race, while Undercover Affair and Rotelle — both natural prominent types — cannot all secure their preferred position and at least one will have to race further back than ideal. This field holds more forward-running types than the shape can accommodate: Jaijai is the clear favourite to lead, God Given Talent and Dance A Jig are best positioned to press her, and Undercover Affair and Rotelle face the squeeze. A race run at an honest but unforced single-pace tempo on a flat five-furlong track in Good conditions strongly favours horses with a prominent or pressing style who can travel smoothly just off the leader and pounce in the final furlong — punishing those forced out of position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jaijai Controls, Pressers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Jaijai leads uncontested at a sustainable gallop and prominent trackers travel smoothly within a length or two.
scenarios.body: Jaijai sets a measured tempo, allowing God Given Talent and Dance A Jig to sit just off her shoulder before launching their challenge in the final furlong; the flat, unrelenting five furlongs at Haydock suits horses who can press the pace and sustain their effort to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Jaijai Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Jaijai sets a pace slow enough that she conserves energy and the prominent challengers cannot find a gear advantage late.
scenarios.body: Levey has the tactical nous to control fractions from the front, and if the tempo is genuinely modest the leader can steal a break into the final furlong that the pressers simply cannot close; Jaijai's five-from-five record at Good going underpins her stamina for the distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Wider Shuffle
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses push forward early and the tempo is sharper than expected, unsettling horses forced back.
scenarios.body: A faster pace compresses the field and those like Rotelle or Undercover Affair who manage to find a front-rank position against expectations become dangerous as the race plays out with genuine pace to run at; Casino Star, mapped to the rear but a natural prominent type, is least likely to benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and late energy proves decisive.
scenarios.body: Casino Star is the only horse mapped to the hold-up position, but is a redistributed prominent type who is unlikely to be travelling in a true closing role; this scenario is materially discounted because there is no genuine hold-up horse in the field to execute it.

watchPoints.text: Watch Jaijai's early stride — if Sean Levey is challenged for the lead in the opening furlong by Undercover Affair or Rotelle, the tempo could lift sharply and fundamentally alter the race shape.

Undercover Affair and Rotelle are both natural prominent horses who cannot all get to their preferred position; monitor which one is forced to check or ease back as the field settles, as that horse's chance diminishes significantly.
God Given Talent drops from 6f to 5f for the first time — if the shorter trip finds her out too quickly or she fails to settle in the prominent position, Dance A Jig is well placed to capitalise.

Casino Star is shown at the rear but is not a genuine hold-up type; if she appears to be travelling strongly in the early stages it likely means the pace is slow enough for all horses to coast — watch the early gallop fractions as a signal of the whole race shape.

races.name: Zyn Frontrunner Finish EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Zyn Strong Stride EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Find Your Zyn Moment Stride Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Distinct Spirit
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has won his last two starts over a mile on Good, handled by Kubler yard firing at 4/11 in the past fortnight; drops back to seven furlongs which is the question, but his prominent style puts him ideally placed if Farandaway sets a sensible pace.
runners_data.comment: Distinct Spirit arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, making him a potent threat at 140 lb; the short six-day turnaround is the one question mark his connections must answer.

runners_data.name: Farandaway
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's four-year-old is the sole confirmed front-runner and carries the race's tactical blueprint on her back; only 1/7 for the yard lately but her going record at Good is modest (6/15 similar-going entries), and if she is caught on a below-par day she could empty sharply.
runners_data.comment: Farandaway arrives in fine nick — a winner two starts back and placed last time out, returning after just 15 days — and has experience over today's trip and going. The main risk is whether 135 lb blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Montezin
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain sends this one out 13 days after a run, tongue-strap applied, but a sequence of mid-table finishes (4th, 4th, 8th, 5th) at longer trips suggests he needs improvement when reverting to seven furlongs at this level.
runners_data.comment: Montezin shaped with promise when fourth three starts back and returns here just 13 days later with experience over today's trip and going; winless in his last five starts, but our ratings just about favour him and he looks the one to beat from stall 2 off 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Criminal Shore
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's hold-up specialist carries a visor and has a course-and-distance win at Southwell on the cv; this is his natural style in full, but he needs a genuinely strong gallop to deliver a telling late thrust at Haydock and the likely controlled tempo is a real concern.
runners_data.comment: Criminal Shore won three starts back but has since posted an unplaced effort and a sixth, and his speed rating of 69 leaves him vulnerable against stronger rivals; he has run over today's distance and going before, though stall ten and 134 lb are notable asks.

runners_data.name: Raffles Angel
runners_data.note: Jack Jones runner who has placed in three of her last four starts, all over six furlongs at Good; stepping up to seven today is the key unknown, though her prominent style means she will be in the mix if the trip is within her compass.
runners_data.comment: Twice third in her last two starts, Raffles Angel arrives here in decent nick after just 15 days, has experience over today's trip and conditions, yet remains winless in her last five — her consistency keeps her in the mix, though breaking through looks the challenge.

runners_data.name: Potomac River
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for TJ Kent, ridden by Jack Mitchell, whose recent form includes a couple of respectable efforts over seven furlongs on Good; a dependable gallop-setter would suit him but a slow pace leaves him with too much to do.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a sixth last time out, Potomac River has hit a flat patch in form and ranks ninth of eleven on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, but little in his recent profile makes him easy to recommend from stall 11 off 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Evocative Spark
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with three recent wins over six and seven furlongs at Good, visor retained — in terms of form, he is well-qualified, but this field's congestion forces him to race further back than his natural prominent style demands, diluting his chance materially.
runners_data.comment: Evocative Spark has winning form in his recent starts — a winner two starts back and two further wins in his last six — yet a seventh three starts back and a fourth last time out temper expectations, and 69 days off the track is a fitness query at 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Tokyo Joe
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's four-year-old is trained by one of the meeting's in-form handlers (10/38 over 14 days) and has a recent win over eight furlongs; his true front-running tendencies mean the midfield slot he is likely to occupy is not where he wants to be, blunting his realistic prospects.
runners_data.comment: Tokyo Joe arrives on the back of a win last time out, and his trainer is in cracking form at 26% over the past fortnight — he's a serious threat here; the main concern is whether 131 lb from stall seven blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Invincible Ruby
runners_data.note: Three wins from eleven starts on Good for Iain Jardine's four-year-old, most coming over six furlongs; being pushed back from his preferred prominent position by the sheer number of like-minded horses in this field means he faces an uphill task finding his rhythm.
runners_data.comment: Invincible Ruby ran second last time out and has a win two starts back, showing consistent recent form, though she carries a stiff 129 lb from stall 9 and ranks seventh of eleven on ratings — in-form but up against it on weight.

runners_data.name: Magic Music
runners_data.note: Steph Hollinshead's runner has been absent 42 days and drops from a win back to a placing zone in recent runs; a natural pace-pressing type who will find himself tracking in unfamiliar midfield territory, making the layoff and positional compromise a double burden.
runners_data.comment: Magic Music has not recaptured her winning form since a victory two starts back, finishing sixth last time out, and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures she faces a stiff ask here — though she has run over today's trip and going before and stall one gets her away cleanly.

runners_data.name: Bajan Bandit
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 60, best form coming over a mile on Tapeta at Wolverhampton — the step down to seven on turf at Haydock looks sharp on both trip and class, and having his front-running tendencies displaced further compounds his already difficult task.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked last of 11 on our figures, Bajan Bandit does at least return after 31 days and has run over today's trip and going before — but a run of three consecutive sixth-place finishes and a fifth two starts back make him hard to fancy here.

races.paceDynamic: Farandaway is the one confirmed front-runner in this seven-furlong Haydock handicap and, with no genuine rival likely to match her stride-for-stride from the gates, she is set to control proceedings at a sustainable gallop on good ground. The redistribution flag matters here: Evocative Spark, Tokyo Joe, Invincible Ruby, Magic Music and Bajan Bandit are all natural prominent racers who cannot all occupy their preferred position behind the leader, meaning several will be shuffled back into an uncharacteristic midfield role and race with their tactical hands tied. Distinct Spirit, Raffles Angel and Montezin are the horses most likely to actually lock up the prominent slots behind Farandaway, as they are neither redistributed nor flagged out of role. With a single, uncontested pace-setter likely to dictate a controlled tempo, this race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently in the slipstream and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — hold-up horses are likely to find the pace insufficient to generate the late gaps they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Farandaway Controls Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Farandaway leads without meaningful early pressure and sets a measured, even gallop over the seven furlongs.
scenarios.body: Farandaway dictates on her own terms, keeping the pace honest but not punishing, and the race resolves into a stamina-test for those who tracked her throughout; horses who secured prominent berths early have first run in the straight and can sustain their effort to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Land Running
scenarios.trigger: If Distinct Spirit and Raffles Angel sit tight behind Farandaway and she drops away late, handing the race to those with most cover.
scenarios.body: The steady pace allows both hold-their-position types to conserve energy before unleashing a sustained challenge from two furlongs out; the finishing straight at Haydock rewards those who have not wasted early speed chasing a runaway.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Farandaway goes too fast early against her instincts or is briefly pressured, setting up a race for genuine hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A burning first half-mile leaves the front end empty inside the final two furlongs, creating room for Criminal Shore and Potomac River to pick up the pieces from off the pace; both are true hold-up types who welcome a true gallop to aim at.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scrimmage Suits Scrambler
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types are bumped and baulked early, turning the race into a messy scramble with multiple moves from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: With pace compressed and horses bunched in the straight, a horse like Evocative Spark — experienced at threading through fields having won over course-relevant trips — could find a gap when others are blocked; form at Good going repeatedly supports its ability to accelerate in a muddling finish.

watchPoints.text: Distinct Spirit has won his last two starts prominently on Good ground and is trained by a yard striking at 4/11 over 14 days — if he settles immediately behind Farandaway he is the biggest danger to turning this into a procession for the tracked pair.

Farandaway is the lone pace-maker but has only a 6/15 strike-rate on similar going — monitor whether she is travelling sweetly in the early stages, because any sign of struggle will collapse the controlled scenario the race shape is built around.

With five horses (Evocative Spark, Tokyo Joe, Invincible Ruby, Magic Music, Bajan Bandit) all competing for midfield slots they would not naturally choose, watch for a messy, compressed pack forming early that could cause interference and knock the expected race shape sideways.

Criminal Shore and Potomac River are the only genuine hold-up horses in the field — if Farandaway is briefly challenged and the gallop accelerates into a proper true test, both come into play, but neither should be expected to fire on a steady tempo.

Tokyo Joe's trainer Ed Walker is operating at 10/38 over 14 days — if Tokyo Joe breaks sharply and instinctively tries to press towards the front despite his redistributed position, he could disrupt Farandaway's control and materially alter the race's complexion.
